sources.entry: Privacy Redirect for Safari - Redirect Twitter, YouTube, Reddit, Google Maps, Google Search, and Google Translate to privacy friendly alternatives.

summary.one_liner: A Safari web extension for macOS and iOS that redirects links from Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, Google services and Medium to privacy-friendly alternatives.
summary.what_it_does: The extension intercepts browsing to Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, Google Translate, Google Maps, Google Search and Medium and redirects those pages to privacy-friendly alternatives. It is described as configurable. It is a fork of Simon Brazell's Privacy Redirect, rewritten in SwiftUI and JavaScript for macOS and iOS. The README points to an App Store download and says it requires macOS 11 or later, or iOS 15 or later. The README does not name the specific alternative front-ends it redirects to.
use_cases: avoid tracking when opening YouTube links in Safari
redirect Twitter or Reddit links to alternative front-ends
keep Google Search and Maps use more private on Mac or iPhone
stop Medium and Instagram links from loading on mainstream sites
configure which sites get redirected in Safari
how_to_run: Install from the Mac App Store or iOS App Store (link in README)
Enable the extension in Safari settings
notable: Fork of Simon Brazell's Privacy Redirect, rewritten in SwiftUI and JavaScript
Runs on both macOS and iOS Safari
Covers Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, Google Translate, Google Maps, Google Search and Medium
caveats: Requires macOS 11 or later or iOS 15 or later
Distributed via the App Store; the README does not describe building from source
The README does not name the target alternative services
